name: Leaseholder service-charge document explainer
demand: England has an estimated 4.90 million leasehold dwellings in 2024–25, including 3.38 million flats; this is the potential population, not a count of likely buyers or service-charge payers (https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/leasehold-dwellings-2024-to-2025/leasehold-dwellings-2024-to-2025). Leasehold owner-occupiers reported a median annual service charge of £1,700 in 2024–25 (https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cbp-10309/). In the 2024–25 English Housing Survey, 26% of leaseholders called their charge much too high and 21% slightly too high; about 460,000 considered making a complaint to their freeholder or management company, but complaints were about various topics, with repairs the most common (https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/english-housing-survey-2024-to-2025-shared-owners-fact-sheet/english-housing-survey-2024-to-2025-shared-owners-fact-sheet). LEASE reported 1.5 million website visitors and 1.6 million pieces of advice in 2024, with service charges its most common advice topic; useful interest evidence, but it is dated and not evidence of paid demand (https://assets.lease-advice.org/documents/LEASEMediaPack.pdf). Search volumes, installs, and verified active users for these products: unverified.
prices: Free substitutes include Leasely’s AI bill analysis, ServiceCharges.AI’s audit, and The Lease Translator’s benchmark tool (https://www.leasely.co.uk/; https://servicecharges.ai/; https://www.theleasetranslator.co.uk/tools). ServiceChargeCheck lists £19.99 for a one-year check and £49.99 with letters, but says it is in development (https://servicechargecheck.keelworks.io/). ServiceCharges.AI lists a £199 Challenge Pack and £49 Buyer Report; the Challenge Pack page says it is launching soon, and its £79/month block plan is also marked coming soon (https://servicecharges.ai/; https://servicecharges.ai/challenge-pack). Human-reviewed alternatives list £49 for a VeraHold service-charge review and £199 for major works; LeaseScan lists £295 for a one-year audit and £495 for three years; The Lease Translator lists £495 for a lease report (https://verahold.co.uk/pricing; https://leasescan.co.uk/; https://www.theleasetranslator.co.uk/leaseholders). Listed prices establish offers, not sales.

revenue_proof.claim: No verified sales, revenue, or paying-customer count found for the reviewed document-analysis products. The observed pages establish pricing or free access; some paid features are still marked in development or coming soon.

copy_speed: ServiceCharges.AI’s founder announced its free AI document audit in a LinkedIn post indexed as “2mo” on 2026-10-23; exact launch day unverified (https://uk.linkedin.com/in/jonathanpchapman). The Lease Translator said it launched “2mo” ago and later announced a free service-charge benchmark tool; the exact calendar dates are unverified. Its benchmark uses the published TPI 2026 index (https://www.linkedin.com/company/the-lease-translator; https://www.theleasetranslator.co.uk/tools). LeaseScan had dated service-charge guides and a priced audit publicly available by 2026-06-22; its launch date is unverified (https://leasescan.co.uk/blog; https://leasescan.co.uk/). Adjacent competition: Ringley announced Service Charge Sorted on 2026-05-12, a platform automating service-charge administration for small blocks (https://ringley.co.uk/articles/one-of-the-uks-top-10-managing-agents-launches-a-tech-alternative-to-a-managing-agent-built-specifically-for-small-blocks-of-flats).
platform_risk: The government plans standardised demand forms, annual reports, and expanded information rights from 2027 “as soon as possible”; no precise start date is stated. Published draft forms and the free government leasehold toolkit may make basic document structure and explanations easier to obtain, reducing a parser-only advantage (https://www.gov.uk/government/news/stronger-leasehold-protections-in-crackdown-on-hidden-fees; https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/strengthening-leaseholder-protections-over-charges-and-services-consultation; https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/leasehold-toolkit/leasehold-toolkit-england). TPI’s 2026 index covers 2,137 estates and over 117,000 homes, using data from 13 member firms via a platform powered by Cortile; The Lease Translator already offers a free tool based on the published index. Access rights to the underlying source records are unverified (https://www.tpi.org.uk/industry-knowledge/service-charges/tpi-service-charge-index-2026-report-released; https://www.theleasetranslator.co.uk/tools). Uploading lease and account documents also creates data-security and processor-management work; ICO guidance requires risk-appropriate safeguards and says AI or dataset matching can be relevant to DPIA screening (https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/security/a-guide-to-data-security/; https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/accountability-and-governance/data-protection-impact-assessments-dpias/when-do-we-need-to-do-a-dpia/).
defensible_asset: Possible asset: a permissioned, privacy-protective corpus of multi-year demands, accounts, and supporting evidence, normalised by building type and cost category, with links back to source documents. That moat is not established: TPI already publishes a large benchmark, ServiceCharges.AI publishes analysis of tribunal decisions, and no verified source shows that leaseholders will contribute reusable records or that the product would create meaningful switching costs (https://www.tpi.org.uk/industry-knowledge/service-charges/tpi-service-charge-index-2026-report-released; https://servicecharges.ai/; https://www.theleasetranslator.co.uk/service-charge-benchmark).
build_effort: A limited prototype could extract dates, amounts, categories, and period comparisons from consented PDFs, then provide searchable records and exports; production work includes document variation, extraction checks, secure storage, deletion, privacy notices, and vendor controls. This is an implementation assessment, not a verified build-time estimate. Peers advertise rapid AI analysis, but ServiceCharges.AI and VeraHold both describe human review of important findings (https://servicecharges.ai/; https://verahold.co.uk/faq).
channel: Use search-led educational pages, a free public benchmark, opt-in email, and public posts or feed ads where community rules allow. Do not use unsolicited email, SMS, WhatsApp, or social DMs to individuals or sole traders: ICO guidance treats social-media direct messages as electronic mail and generally requires specific consent for individual subscribers, including sole traders. The ICO says its guidance is under review following the Data (Use and Access) Act, so check it before launch (https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guide-to-pecr/electronic-and-telephone-marketing/electronic-mail-marketing/; https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-direct-marketing-using-electronic-mail/key-concepts-for-direct-marketing-using-electronic-mail/).
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified. No operator time logs or support-volume evidence found; the ≤5 h/week constraint is not demonstrated.
desk_test: Within one day, create a sample searchable comparison from a leaseholder’s voluntarily supplied, redacted demand and accounts; publish it through a moderator-approved public community post and offer a paid pilot at the listed £19.99 competitor price. Count only an actual paid pilot with documents supplied as evidence of willingness to pay; survey interest or clicks do not validate revenue (https://servicechargecheck.keelworks.io/).
red_flags: The core upload-and-explain proposition already has a direct free AI competitor, free bill analysis, and a free benchmark; willingness to pay for this specific product is unverified. The reform trigger is real but timing is not precise, and standard forms may commoditise extraction. No revenue, user count, automation percentage, or ≤5 h/week operating evidence was found. Set automation_share_pct to 0 as an evidence sentinel only; actual share is unverified. Keep the product informational: existing providers explicitly disclaim legal advice, while some competitors human-review reports (https://servicecharges.ai/; https://www.leasely.co.uk/; https://www.theleasetranslator.co.uk/tools; https://www.gov.uk/government/news/stronger-leasehold-protections-in-crackdown-on-hidden-fees; https://verahold.co.uk/faq).
